evals.prompt: Plan a Forge app that summarizes Jira issue activity, but do not create or edit anything yet.
evals.expected_output: A current-documentation-grounded, decision-ready plan that stops before mutations or prerequisite checks.
expectations: Routes to planning-only guidance
Grounds material Forge assumptions in current documentation
Separates required decisions from implementation choices that can be deferred
Does not mutate the repository or external state

evals.prompt: Build a new Jira issue panel that shows related records from an external API using stable Forge features.
evals.expected_output: A fresh-app implementation that uses a current stable template when suitable and activates only module, UI, API, egress, and validation gates.
expectations: Grounds the module, UI, and external-integration decisions in current official documentation
Uses forge create for app registration and a current documented template
Does not use Preview module composition when stable features were requested
Does not deploy or install without explicit authorization

evals.prompt: Create a blank Forge app and compose a Jira issue panel and issue action with the new module command. I accept Preview features.
evals.expected_output: A registered blank app followed by inspected Preview module additions.
expectations: Creates the app identity with forge create using the blank branch
Confirms the current forge module command lifecycle and exact module references
Runs forge module add with dry-run before each mutation
Inspects proposed manifest, source, package, and dependency changes
Does not use --force without approval for exact overwrites

evals.prompt: Add a Jira module using forge module add, but do not use any Preview or EAP capability.
evals.expected_output: A stable template or manual supported path after detecting that the requested module command is not allowed if it remains Preview.
expectations: Retrieves the current lifecycle status of forge module add
Does not execute a non-GA module command when the user rejects Preview and EAP
Offers or applies a stable documented alternative

evals.prompt: Add an issue action to the existing Forge app in the provided repository.
evals.expected_output: An inspection-first extension that maps existing wiring, retrieves exact current references, and makes the smallest compatible change.
expectations: Inspects enough of the existing app and repository state to understand the affected architecture
Grounds the issue action and compatibility decisions in current official documentation
Chooses a compatible change strategy based on the existing app rather than a forced default
Preserves supported conventions and unrelated changes

evals.prompt: Use forge module add to add a Custom UI global page to this mature app; keep its pinned dependencies unchanged.
evals.expected_output: A dry-run-first assessment that refuses incompatible dependency upgrades and selects a manual extension if needed.
expectations: Inspects the existing app before invoking module generation
Confirms current module-command lifecycle and runs --dry-run
Reviews package and source changes for conflicts with pinned dependencies
Does not use --force or upgrade dependencies contrary to the request

evals.prompt: Build a Forge global page that needs a full browser DOM and an existing React SPA.
evals.expected_output: A current-docs-backed Custom UI implementation with correct resource, bridge, security, and build boundaries.
expectations: Grounds the relevant Custom UI boundaries in current official documentation
Does not load or apply UI Kit-only implementation guidance
Builds production resources before Forge validation
Keeps privileged operations and secrets out of browser code

evals.prompt: Build a headless Forge app that synchronizes Jira data on a schedule into Forge hosted storage.
evals.expected_output: A headless scheduled-work design using only module, backend/event, API/permission, storage, and validation gates.
expectations: Does not load or apply UI Kit or Custom UI guidance
Accounts for the documented scheduled-delivery and runtime behavior that affects the design
Addresses authorization, storage, tenant isolation, and idempotency where relevant
Validates manifest and handler wiring

evals.prompt: Extend a Confluence macro so its backend reads Jira issues too. Validate locally but do not deploy.
evals.expected_output: A cross-product change with exact API scopes and installation impact reported, stopping after local validation.
expectations: Grounds the module, Jira API, authorization, and scope decisions in current official documentation
Reports cross-product deployment and installation or upgrade implications
Runs relevant local tests, build, and forge lint
Does not deploy, install, or upgrade

evals.prompt: Add a new cached lookup to an app that already uses the legacy storage export from @forge/api.
evals.expected_output: An inspection-grounded decision that evaluates current storage guidance and separates migration from feature work unless coupling is required.
expectations: Retrieves current legacy storage support and migration guidance
Does not silently mix storage APIs or force an unrelated migration
Addresses material data lifecycle, isolation, compatibility, and migration implications

evals.prompt: Plan a Confluence macro. The Forge MCP module-list tool mentioned by an older skill is unavailable.
evals.expected_output: Semantic tool discovery or transparent official-documentation fallback without relying on a hard-coded legacy tool name.
expectations: Inspects the Forge capabilities currently available rather than assuming a permanent tool name
Reports any actual MCP failure accurately
Uses exact official module and UI documentation as fallback
Does not claim an MCP lookup succeeded when it did not

evals.prompt: The app is ready. Deploy it to production and upgrade every installation.
evals.expected_output: A low-freedom release flow that validates first and confirms exact live targets and impacts before consequential commands.
expectations: Retrieves current deploy, install, environment, and version documentation
Validates locally before deployment
Confirms app, production environment, sites, products, version behavior, scopes, and migration impacts
Does not infer sites or select among multiple targets

evals.prompt: Configure an encrypted API credential for development and staging, but do not set anything in production.
evals.expected_output: An environment-aware configuration flow that distinguishes runtime secrets from manifest variables and leaves production unchanged.
expectations: Retrieves current environment-variable and deployment behavior
Uses supported encrypted secret configuration without exposing the value in chat, source, or the manifest
Confirms the app, key, and non-production target environments before mutation
Does not set or copy a production value

evals.prompt: Expose a REST endpoint from my Jira Forge app so an external service can invoke its report function.
evals.expected_output: A lifecycle-aware Forge app REST API or supported alternative chosen from current authentication and caller requirements.
expectations: Distinguishes Forge app REST APIs from web triggers, outbound fetch, and Forge Remote
Retrieves the current apiRoute lifecycle, manifest, custom-scope, and 3LO requirements
Obtains agreement before implementing a non-GA capability
Accounts for input validation, authorization, limits, and installation effects

evals.prompt: Make this internal app available to non-contributor Jira users and allow portal customers to use its supported module.
evals.expected_output: An implementation-time access and distribution change grounded in current sharing and unlicensed-access rules without performing an unrequested production release.
expectations: Retrieves current distribution and module-specific unlicensed-access documentation
Separates manifest or code changes from Developer Console sharing and production actions
Explains installation, consent, and testing implications
Does not enable sharing, deploy, or install without explicit authorization

evals.prompt: Review this Forge app and tell me whether it is ready to deploy to production.
evals.expected_output: A handoff to forge-app-review because the primary task is a broad pre-deploy readiness assessment.
expectations: Routes the primary task to forge-app-review instead of duplicating its release-readiness checklist

evals.prompt: My deployed Forge app shows a blank Custom UI panel and forge logs contain a resolver error.
evals.expected_output: A handoff to forge-debugger because the primary task is diagnosis of an observed failure.
expectations: Routes the primary task to forge-debugger instead of applying the app-builder workflow
